strength.transition.$description: How the password strength meter animates as it fills.

color.white.$description: Pure white, referenced by the tint half of every colour scale.

color.black.$description: Pure black, referenced by the shade half of every colour scale.

color-mix.space.$description: The interpolation space every generated colour step is mixed in.

color-mix.tint-color.$description: What tints are mixed towards — the light end of every scale.

color-mix.shade-color.$description: What shades are mixed towards — the dark end of every scale.

spacing.base.$description: The base spacer. Every step of the spacing scale is a multiple of it, so changing it rescales the whole system.

spacing.root.$description: Upstream hardcodes this rather than deriving it from $spacer, so changing the base spacer does not move it.

radius.base.$description: The base radius. Every step of the 0–9 scale is a multiple of it, so one change rounds or squares every component at once.

radius.pill.$description: A fixed 50rem, set on $root-tokens after the $radii loop.

grid.columns.$description: How many columns a row divides into. Every `.col-*` class is generated from it, so this is a wider change than it looks.

grid.row-columns.$description: The highest count a `.row-cols-*` layout offers before you have to write your own.

grid.gutter-x.$description: Horizontal gutter between grid columns. It also sets the default container padding, so it decides the page margin too.

grid.gutter-y.$description: Vertical gutter between grid rows. Zero by default, so rows sit flush together unless you opt in.

grid.container-padding-x.$description: Inline padding inside a container, holding content clear of the viewport edge on small screens.

border.width.$description: The default border width. Components reference it rather than hard-coding 1px.

border.style.$description: The default border style. Every component reads it, so switching to `dashed` restyles the whole system rather than one element.

border.bg.$description: A border the colour of the page — used to punch a gap between adjacent filled elements.

border.body.$description: The standard visible border. Stronger than `subtle`, calmer than `emphasized`.

border.muted.$description: A quieter border for grouping without drawing a line the eye stops at.

border.subtle.$value: light-dark(color-mix(in oklch, var(--gray-100), var(--gray-200)), color-mix(in oklch, var(--gray-800), var(--gray-900)))
border.subtle.$description: The faintest border. For separating areas that are already distinguished by space.

border.emphasized.$description: A deliberately visible border, for focus targets and selected states.

border.white.$description: Fixed white in both schemes, for an edge that must stay light whatever the theme does.

border.black.$description: Fixed black in both schemes, for an edge that must stay dark whatever the theme does.

border.width-keyline.$description: A sub-pixel hairline for dividers that should read as a seam rather than a border.

border.color.$description: The default border colour, for anything that does not choose a more specific one.

border.color-translucent.$description: A border mixed from the foreground rather than a fixed grey, so it works over any surface underneath.

control.checked-bg.$description: Fill of a checkbox, radio or switch once it is on.

control.checked-border-color.$description: Border of a checked control. Follows the checked fill unless you separate them.

control.active-bg.$description: Fill of a control while it is being pressed.

control.active-border-color.$description: Border of a control while it is being pressed. Follows the active fill unless you set the two apart.

control.disabled-bg.$description: Fill of a control that cannot be used. Combined with the disabled opacity below, so the two compound.

control.disabled-opacity.$description: How far a disabled control fades. Applied on top of the disabled fill, so both compound.

control.transition-duration.$description: How long a checkbox or radio mark takes to appear.

control.transition-timing.$description: Easing for a checkbox or radio mark. Overshoots slightly, so the mark pops rather than slides.

control.field.fg.$description: Text colour shared by buttons and form fields, so an unstyled button matches an input beside it.

control.field.bg.$description: Background shared by buttons and form fields. Variants paint over it; this is what an unstyled control shows.

control.field.gap.$description: Space between a control’s icon and its label.

control.field.min-height.$description: Minimum height of a button or form field. This is what sets the vertical rhythm of a form.

control.field.padding-y.$description: Vertical padding inside a button or form field.

control.field.padding-x.$description: Horizontal padding inside a button or form field.

control.field.font-size.$description: Text size inside a button or form field.

control.field.line-height.$description: Leading inside a button or form field. Together with the padding it decides how tall the control ends up.

control.field.border-radius.$description: Corner rounding on a button or form field. Taken from the radius scale, so it moves when the base radius does.

control.field.xs.gap.$description: Space between a control’s icon and its label at the extra-small size.

control.field.xs.min-height.$description: Minimum height of a button or form field at the extra-small size. This is what sets the vertical rhythm of a form.

control.field.xs.padding-y.$description: Vertical padding inside a button or form field at the extra-small size.

focus.width.$description: Thickness of the focus ring. Do not go below 2px: this is the only cue a keyboard user gets.

focus.offset.$description: Gap between a control and its focus ring, so the ring stays legible against the control.

focus.color.$description: Colour of the focus ring. Follows the primary role by default.

focus.ring.$description: The whole focus ring shorthand, composed from the width and colour above.

motion.timing-overlay.$description: Shared easing for overlays — dialogs, drawers and menus — so they all enter with the same character.

bg.body.$description: The page background. Every other surface is measured against it.

bg.1.$description: The first raised surface — card headers, table stripes, anything a step above the page.

bg.2.$description: A second step up, for a surface raised above one that is already raised.

bg.3.$description: A third step, used mostly for disabled controls and inset wells.

bg.4.$description: The strongest neutral fill before you reach an inverted surface.

bg.fg.$description: The foreground colour used as a background — for inverted blocks that flip the page around.

bg.white.$description: Fixed white in both schemes. Use it when a surface must not follow the theme.

bg.black.$description: Fixed black in both schemes. Use it when a surface must not follow the theme.

bg.transparent.$description: No background at all. Use it to clear an inherited one.

bg.inherit.$description: Take whatever background the parent has. A CSS-wide keyword, so it cannot be stored in a custom property.

fg.body.$description: Primary body text. The default reading colour.

fg.1.$description: Slightly de-emphasised text — secondary lines that still have to be read comfortably.

fg.2.$description: Supporting text: captions, helper text under a field, table metadata.

fg.3.$description: Faint text for labels and placeholders. Below WCAG AA for body copy, so keep it off long prose.

fg.4.$description: The faintest step, for decorative or disabled text only. It does not meet WCAG AA at any size.

fg.bg.$description: The page background used as a text colour — for text on an inverted surface.

fg.white.$description: Fixed white in both schemes, for text that must stay light whatever the theme does.

fg.black.$description: Fixed black in both schemes, for text that must stay dark whatever the theme does.

fg.inherit.$description: Take whatever text colour the parent has.

theme-color.primary.border.$description: A primary border against the page background — tinted enough to read as primary, calm enough not to compete with the fill.

type.body.font-family.$description: The body font stack. It deliberately omits `system-ui`, which resolves to the locale’s UI font and renders non-Latin text incorrectly.

type.body.font-size.$description: Base text size. Component sizes that reference it follow; the fluid heading scale does not.

type.body.font-weight.$description: Weight of ordinary running text. Headings set their own, so this governs paragraphs and labels.

type.body.line-height.$description: Leading for running text. Headings override it, so this mostly decides how dense a paragraph feels.

type.heading.color.$description: Heading colour. Inherits by default, so headings match body text unless you separate them.

type.hr.border-color.$description: Colour of a horizontal rule, and of the divider inside an alert or a card.

type.link.color.$description: Link colour. Uses the solid brand colour in light mode and the lighter text variant in dark.

type.link.decoration.$description: How a link is marked. Removing the underline leaves colour as the only cue, which fails for readers who cannot distinguish it.

type.link.underline-offset.$description: How far the underline sits below the text. Enough clearance keeps it from cutting through descenders.

type.link.hover-color.$description: Link colour on hover — the base colour darkened, so the shift reads without changing hue.

type.code.font-family.$value: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, 'Cascadia Mono', Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace
type.code.font-family.$description: The monospace stack, for code and any figure that should align in columns.

type.code.font-size.$description: Code size relative to its surrounding text, so inline code does not tower over the line.

type.code.color.$description: Colour of inline code, set a step away from running text so it reads as a quotation.
